articles.title: Architectural Deep-Dive: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
articles.excerpt: Eliminating Privileged-Correction Contamination in Multimodal RLVR with Visual-Attribution Gating Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ha…
articles.body: Eliminating Privileged-Correction Contamination in Multimodal RLVR with Visual-Attribution Gating Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) have established themselves as standard approaches for post-training advanced reasoning models. While task-level outcome supervision works exceptionally well for formal domains like competitive programming or symbolic math, it exhibits severe structural limitations when applied to multimodal agents performing fine-grained visual reasoning. When an agent fails to locate a coordinate or misinterprets an engineering blueprint, scalar outcome rewards fail to indicate which specific intermediate reasoning token introduced the error.

articles.excerpt: When people ask, "Why build another messenger when WhatsApp and Telegram already exist?", my answer is simple: we lost the simplicity. Modern messaging apps have become bloated mini-operating systems…
articles.body: Hey! I’m an independent software creator documenting the build process of Weby. When people ask, "Why build another messenger when WhatsApp and Telegram already exist?", my answer is simple: we lost the simplicity. Modern messaging apps have become bloated mini-operating systems packed with stories, crypto wallets, endless algorithmic feeds, and invasive analytics. I wanted to build something different: A messenger that opens in less than a second on any device. Zero battery drain and zero background surveillance. Instant Web access without scanning QR codes or forced installs. Crystal-clear, encrypted P2P voice and video calls.

articles.title: A Low Search CTR Is Not a Title Problem Until This Test Says It Is
articles.excerpt: A Low Search CTR Is Not a Title Problem Until This Test Says It Is A page can lose clicks while its title is perfectly adequate. Its average position may have shifted. Google may have attributed impre…
articles.body: A Low Search CTR Is Not a Title Problem Until This Test Says It Is A page can lose clicks while its title is perfectly adequate. Its average position may have shifted. Google may have attributed impressions to a different canonical. The query mix may have broadened from high-intent searches to research queries. Mobile traffic may have increased. A rich result, local pack, shopping unit or AI-generated answer may have changed what users see. Brand demand may have weakened. The page may simply have too few impressions for its click-through rate to be stable. Yet the usual response is immediate: rewrite the title, add a number, insert a stronger adjective, and wait for the graph to rise. That is not a diagnosis. It is an intervention without a causal model.

articles.body: 회의실 장비 후보를 비교할 때 화면이 잘 읽히는지와 보관하기 편한지를 똑같이 중요하게 볼 필요는 없습니다. 항목별 점수에 중요도를 곱해 더하면 무엇을 더 중요하게 봤는지 드러나는 비교표를 만들 수 있습니다. 이번에는 가상 후보 A·B·C를 네 항목으로 비교합니다. 처음 중요도에서는 A안 3.80점, B·C안 3.70점입니다. 연결 준비의 비중을 높이면 B안 4.10점이 됩니다. 입력표·수식·완성 결과와 빈 재사용 틀을 본문만으로 구성합니다. 이 글의 본문은 AI가 작성하고 DEV 형식으로 재구성한 합성 예제입니다. 후보·점수·가중치는 설명용 설정이며 실제 상품 평가나 구매 추천, 장비 사용 경험이 아닙니다. 1. 평가할 항목과 점수의 뜻 정하기 여기서 가중치는 항목의 중요도입니다. 화면 글자 읽기를 40%, 보관·이동을 10%로 두면 같은 1점 차이도 앞 항목에 네 배의 비중을 줍니다. 먼저 네 가지 질문을 정하고 모든 후보에 같은 질문을 적용합니다. [네 항목의 질문] 화면 글자 읽기: 회의 자료의 글자를 읽기 편한가? 연결 준비: 회의 시작 전에 연결을 준비하기 편한가? 조작 편의: 자주 쓰는 기능을 선택하고 바꾸기 편한가? 보관·이동: 사용 뒤 정리하고 옮기기 편한가? 점수는 1~5의 정수이며 클수록 이 예제에서 더 유리합니다. 1점은 해당 사용 조건에 맞지 않음, 3점은 일부 보완이 있으면 사용 가능, 5점은 추가 보완 없이 조건에 맞음으로 정합니다. 2점과 4점은 각각 그 사이 수준입니다. 이것은 자체 판단 척도입니다. 실제로 쓸 때는 어떤 보완이 필요한지와 점수를 정한 근거를 항목별로 적으세요.

articles.title: Indexing 27,854 near-identical pages without tripping duplicate-content filters
articles.excerpt: Programmatic SEO is a bet: that you can generate thousands of pages from a template and have Google treat them as genuinely useful rather than thin duplicates. We run a long-distance moving cost site…
articles.body: Programmatic SEO is a bet: that you can generate thousands of pages from a template and have Google treat them as genuinely useful rather than thin duplicates. We run a long-distance moving cost site with 27,854 route pages, one for every major city pair, and getting them indexed without tripping duplicate-content filters was the whole game. Here is what worked. The duplicate-content problem Every route page answers the same question: how much does it cost to move from City A to City B? The template is identical. The risk is obvious: Google sees 27,854 pages with the same structure and similar text, decides they are duplicates, and indexes a fraction of them. Early on, that is exactly what happened. Thousands of pages sat in "Crawled, currently not indexed" limbo.
articles.author: Daniel Mercer

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan Explanation: This is an unusual rainbow. For one thing, the rainbow is not complete, appearing only in a sunlit fan — but that by itself is not very unusual. What is most unusual is the fake location of the Sun . The Sun appears to be toward the front, just below those hills — but it is not. That is not how rainbows work . Rainbows involve a backward reflection from falling rain , so that the Sun must really be behind you .

articles.body: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

articles.excerpt: Brick by brick ... the truth is out there. You can now own a little piece of that with this 1,478-piece Lego set
articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
